title: The human ideogram on GRCh38 and GRCh37: the cytogenetic bands of chromosomes 1-22, X and Y at the ISCN band levels of 400, 550 and 850 bands per haploid set, with their Giemsa stains and their coordinates on each assembly; and UCSC's cytoBand tables of hg38 and hg19
provider: National Center for Biotechnology Information (NCBI), Genome Decoration Page (ideogram files of the primary assembly units GCF_000001305.16, GRCh38, and GCF_000001305.13, GRCh37); University of California, Santa Cruz, Genome Browser (cytoBand of hg38 and hg19)
credit: Bands: NCBI Genome Decoration Page; UCSC Genome Browser

format: NCBI: tab-separated, a header line beginning with '#', then one band a line: chromosome, arm (p or q), band (as 36.33), ISCN start and stop (the ideogram's own length units), base-pair start and stop (1-based, closed), stain (gneg, gpos, acen, gvar, stalk) and density (25, 50, 75, 100 for gpos). UCSC: tab-separated chrom, chromStart, chromEnd (0-based, half-open), name, gieStain (gneg, gpos25-gpos100, acen, gvar, stalk). On 2026-11-01 UCSC's table and NCBI's 850 level held the same 862 bands with the same coordinates and stains. NCBI's files are not consistent in their base-pair starts: some give the first base of a band (1-based), others the previous band's stop (0-based), and the GRCh37 file of the 850-band level carries no densities; the reader takes each start from its neighbour (genomics/karyotype/bands.hpp), and the GRCh37 850 level is read from UCSC's hg19 table, whose coordinates are the same.
coverage: Homo sapiens, GRCh38 (GCF_000001305.16, the primary assembly unit; its 850-band file is identical to that of GCF_000001305.14) and GRCh37 (GCF_000001305.13); chromosomes 1-22, X and Y, each covered by its bands from its first base to its last without gaps. The 300-band level is not published by NCBI.
licence: NCBI places no restrictions on the use or distribution of its data (https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/home/about/policies/). UCSC Genome Browser tables derived from public data are freely available (https://genome.ucsc.edu/conditions.html). The files are fetched into the cache and not redistributed.
